failedGraders: judge:A consumer for the integration.shared.integration.deactivated integration event was just added to the Go worker: a handler at packages/api/go/internal/sync/handlers/integration_deactivated_handler.go (+ test), a new FindActiveByIntegration read on the syncjob repository (packages/api/go/internal/sync/repositories/syncjob/), and wiring in packages/api/go/internal/sync/module.go. Verify ALL of: (a) CONTRACTS BINDING — the handler's EventName() returns the generated wire constant (wire.IntegrationDeactivatedIntegrationEventName, never a string literal) and Handle decodes the payload into the generated wire.IntegrationDeactivatedIntegrationEvent through an UnmarshalIntegrationEvent entry point; the handler file defines NO local struct with json tags mirroring the wire shape and re-declares no event name constant; on a decode/type mismatch it returns an error rather than silently dropping. (b) DI-REG — the handler is fx.Provide-d AND registered with the ExternalMediator (em.Register / ext.Register) via fx.Invoke in internal/sync/module.go — NOT with the InternalMediator (that mediator carries in-process domain events; this event arrives from the external transport); a compile-time interface assertion for the new handler (var _ ... IntegrationEventHandler = (*...IntegrationDeactivatedHandler)(nil)) exists in the handler file or module.go. (c) TELL-DONT-ASK + PERSISTENCE — the cancellation is find → Cancel() → Save: it loads the integration's active jobs through FindActiveByIntegration, transitions each via the SyncJob aggregate's own Cancel() method, and persists via the repository's Save — no direct .Status = assignment outside the entity, no bulk UPDATE statement that flips status in SQL, no SQL or *sql.DB usage inside the handler. The new FindActiveByIntegration implementation lives on the Pg repository, goes through the repository's querier/TxFromContext helper (UnitOfWork-aware, not a bare r.db), reuses the existing selectCols + scan helpers, and filters status with the enums.SyncStatusPending / enums.SyncStatusRunning constants — not inline 'PENDING'/'RUNNING' string literals in SQL or Go. (d) IDEMPOTENCY / ASYNC — an event for an integration with zero active jobs returns nil (clean no-op, safe redelivery); infrastructure errors (repo read/save failures) are returned so the transport can retry; cancellation runs synchronously inside Handle. (e) TESTS — the handler test constructs the event the way the integration_activated_handler_test.go exemplar does (raw-payload fake or typed construction), uses in-memory fakes for the repository (no DATABASE_URL / DB connection), and covers at least the happy path (active jobs end cancelled and saved) plus the no-active-jobs no-op; the new repository read has coverage in syncjob_pg_test.go following the existing openTestDB skip-without-DATABASE_URL idiom. Scope notes — judge the idiom, not the variable name: BOTH decode spellings are canon — wire.UnmarshalIntegrationEvent(provider.GetPayload()) plus a type assertion (the activated exemplar) OR the generic types.UnmarshalIntegrationEvent[wire.IntegrationDeactivatedIntegrationEvent](event) — do not fail one for not being the other. Delegating the cancellation to a small use case (handler → use case → repository) is as valid as the handler driving the repository directly — judge the find→Cancel→save shape wherever it lives. The quoted event-name JSON inside the TEST file (raw-payload fake parity) is expected — the string-literal ban applies only to the handler's EventName(). fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err) wrapping is the house Go idiom for infrastructure errors — do not demand typed BaseError codes for them (typed codes are for business conditions, and this slice may not need any new ones). Extending the existing integration-activated fx.Invoke with a second handler parameter OR adding a separate fx.Invoke are both canonical. Do not require a detached goroutine — the activated handler's goroutine exists because backfills are long-running; cancellation is short and synchronous. Returning a nil or empty slice from FindActiveByIntegration when nothing matches are both fine (the (nil, nil) not-found canon applies to single-row finds). Inspect the new handler + test, the syncjob repository folder, and internal/sync/module.go. Pre-existing handlers and module wiring are out of scope except where the new registration touches them.
